patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of the observed spend change is tied to shifts in PA-required classification and one unmapped facility bucket rather than a confirmed change in demand or reimbursement. The signal is concentrated in NY, CT, and CA / GA / OH / VA, with the biggest provider concentrations at NYU Langone and Yale New Haven. Business action on utilization or contracting should wait until the PA and facility mapping logic is reconciled.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the PA or facility fields moved, the organization could misdirect UM and reimbursement actions at the wrong providers or products.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped claims to source PA-required and facility type logic in CT, NY, and CA / GA / OH / VA, then rerun provider and product comparisons before taking UM or reimbursement action.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Multiple groups are explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shift and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: NY AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about $3.9M, led by NYU Langone at $2.7M and cervical spinal fusion with CC at $1.1M.
CT AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about $2.8M and is concentrated at Yale New Haven.
CA / GA / OH / VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION was net +$2.5M, led by IU Health Methodist at $1.1M and Henrico at $1.0M, with some offsetting negatives.
A CA PPO Not Mapped facility bucket added about $161K, indicating facility classification cleanup is also needed.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CT PPO acute hospital inpatient spend
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO acute hospital spend rose sharply at Yale New Haven Hospital, with pressure coming from both PA-required and non-PA cases. This is not a pure utilization story: admissions increased and paid per admit also moved higher. The mix suggests a combined UM and reimbursement issue rather than a single lever.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A single provider concentration of this size can materially move CT inpatient cost trend and needs a targeted response.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a joint UM and network review on Yale CT PPO acute admissions, focusing on PA routing, admission criteria, level of care, and reimbursement terms for the highest-cost digestive cases.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Both PA-required and non-PA claims contributed materially at the same provider, so PA flag assignment should be confirmed alongside utilization and rate review.
evidence_summary: Yale New Haven PA-required PPO acute cases added about $3.8M with 38 more admissions and roughly $9K higher paid per admit.
Yale non-PA PPO acute cases added about $0.8M with 43 more admissions and roughly $3K higher paid per admit.
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC added about $235K on 4 admissions with roughly $59K higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: NY EPO acute hospital spend increased mainly in PA-required cases and is heavily concentrated at NYU Langone. The largest identifiable clinical driver is cervical spinal fusion, where the case count and paid per admit both rose. This looks like a focused provider and procedure pressure point rather than a broad NY inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Concentrated EPO inpatient growth at one flagship provider can quickly become a recurring cost issue if not addressed early.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a provider-level inpatient audit at NYU Langone for PA-required EPO admissions, pairing medical-necessity review with reimbursement review for cervical fusion and other high-cost surgical stays.
patterns_data.validation_reason: A meaningful share of the increase is concentrated in low-volume surgical cells, so PA status and claim classification should be confirmed before broader contract action.
evidence_summary: NYU Langone added about $2.8M in PA-required EPO acute cases with 25 more admissions and roughly $31K higher paid per admit.
Cervical spinal fusion with CC added about $379K on 5 admissions with roughly $76K higher paid per admit.
One IU Health Methodist case added about $244K but is a single-admission outlier.

This is an early-warning provider economics pattern that can be addressed before it becomes a broader trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Small but recurring provider-product spikes can compound quickly and often indicate contract, referral, or pre-service control gaps.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Create a targeted provider-product watchlist for contract review and pre-service controls, prioritizing IU Health Methodist, Henrico, NYU Langone, and Ohio State where paid per admit spiked off small baselines.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Many contributing cells are low-baseline or small-volume, so provider and product configuration should be confirmed before broad repricing or policy changes.
evidence_summary: GA POS acute hospital at IU Health Methodist added about $0.9M with 3 more admissions and roughly $228K higher paid per admit.
VA PPO acute hospital at Henrico added about $0.5M with 2 more admissions and roughly $24K higher paid per admit.
CA PPO acute hospital added about $1.4M across IU Health Methodist, NYU Langone, and Henrico, including both PA-required and non-PA cases.

patterns_data.pattern_details: This is a focused outlier case-mix pattern, not a broad inpatient trend. Spend is being driven by a small number of rare, very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases across NY and CA / GA / OH / VA, frequently with only 1 to 3 admissions and six-figure paid per admit. The main business need is case-level clinical and outlier management, not broad benefit or policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A handful of rare surgical or complex medical cases can distort trend and require a different response than routine utilization growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route these episodes to case-level clinical and outlier review to confirm DRG and diagnosis accuracy, assess stop-loss or catastrophic exposure, and separate one-time events from repeatable management opportunities.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most contributing cases are small-volume, low-baseline events with unusually high paid per admit.
evidence_summary: NY rare IP Med/Surg outliers added about $2.6M, including ulcer of intestine digestive MCC at about $469K and coronary bypass at NYU Langone at about $448K.
CA / GA / OH / VA rare IP Med/Surg cases added about $2.5M, led by Ohio State wound debridement and skin graft at about $401K and cardiothoracic surgery at about $384K.
NY / VA cardiac valve procedures without cath with MCC added about $1.0M across NYU Langone and Henrico.
Most contributing cases involved 1 to 3 admissions with six-figure paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Catastrophic airway and transplant episodes need dedicated case management
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IP Med/Surg catastrophic tracheostomy, prolonged ventilation, sepsis, and transplant cases in CT, GA, VA
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: A small number of catastrophic airway and transplant episodes generated very large spend increases across Yale, Henrico, and IU Health Methodist. These are specialized cases with extremely high paid per admit and very low volumes, so they need individual case handling rather than broad utilization policy changes. The presence of tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation and transplant cases points to the need for catastrophic case management and contract carve-out review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Catastrophic cases can overwhelm normal trend management and often depend on specialized clinical, authorization, and reimbursement workflows.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch case-level review for tracheostomy, prolonged ventilation, sepsis, and kidney transplant episodes, including catastrophic case management, transplant authorization, and contract carve-out validation.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increases are driven by rare, small-count cases with very high paid per admit.
evidence_summary: Yale New Haven tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation and sepsis added about $1.4M across 2 admissions, or about $702K paid per admit.
IU Health Methodist added about $509K from a single tracheostomy-related case.
Kidney transplant cases in GA / VA added about $441K across 2 admissions at Henrico and IU Health Methodist.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Maternity and NICU acuity is emerging through C-section-linked neonatal severity and maternal complications
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IP NICU and IP OB delivery/well newborn maternity spend in GA, VA, NY
key_driver_codes: Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate
patterns_data.pattern_details: Maternity-related acuity is showing up through NICU respiratory distress and extreme prematurity in GA / VA, plus severe pre-eclampsia in NY. The largest concentration is at Henrico, where neonatal cases tied to C-section births drove most of the increase. This is a focused maternity and newborn severity pattern that warrants OB and NICU review, not a broad inpatient response.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternal and neonatal high-acuity cases have different clinical and care-management levers than general Med/Surg utilization.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Conduct a combined OB and NICU review of maternal complications and neonatal respiratory distress, with focus on C-section-linked NICU severity and opportunities for maternity case management.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is concentrated in small numbers of high-acuity maternity and neonatal admissions.
evidence_summary: GA / VA NICU extreme immaturity or respiratory distress added about $636K, led by Henrico at about $503K across 4 admissions tied to C-section births.
NY severe pre-eclampsia in IP OB delivery/well newborn added about $38K across 2 admissions.
These are low-volume but high-acuity maternity and newborn cases rather than a broad obstetric utilization shift.
